match_incidents: For this task, you will be given an incident label and its news text.  Then I will provide a list of other candidate incidents and their corresponding news text, along with their IDs.  You must decide if any of the listed candidate incidents is actually the same as the given incident, or if they are related somehow as part of each other.
match_incidents_format: To format your answer, please simply choose one or more incident indexes and place them in between <INCIDENT></INCIDENT>.  In the end, you provide a list in the form of <LIST><INCIDENT></INCIDENT><NEXT>...</LIST> where each incident is separated by <NEXT>.  For example (ignoring the list rules for now), if you believe the first candidate is the same incident, you would write: <INCIDENT>0</INCIDENT><SAME>.  If you believe the first candidate is actually a larger incident and encompasses the given incident, you would write: <INCIDENT>0</INCIDENT><PARENT>.  If you believe the first candidate is actually a smaller incident and is part of the given incident, you would write: <INCIDENT>0</INCIDENT><CHILD>.  If you do not believe any of the candidates are the same incident, please write: <INCIDENT>-1</INCIDENT>.  In addition, in a few sentences ALWAYS describe your reason for the choice of <SAME>, <PARENT> or <CHILD>, and place this in between <WHY></WHY>.  For example if you have multiple incidents chosen, it would be formatted like so: <LIST><INCIDENT>1</INCIDENT><PARENT><WHY>This incident encompasses the given incident because...</WHY><NEXT><INCIDENT>2</INCIDENT><SAME><WHY>This incident is the same as incident 2 because ...</WHY></LIST>.  Remember to use always use <LIST></LIST> even if you only have one incident chosen, though you may feel free to list multiple.  When choosing the larger incident, please select the most relevant (e.g. for an incident about a wildfire, your parent class should be an incident about a wildfire as well if possible)
